# Held-out evaluation pilot

Run `node scripts/model_fidelity_eval.mjs tests/fixtures/model-fidelity/held-out-17/input.json` from the repository root. The output includes the SHA-256 digest of the exact input. Keep each revised input and result under a new name; do not replace a prior run. This input pins six synthetic variants and two planned arms per case. The method arm loads `skills/model-fidelity/SKILL.md`; the control arm does not. Both must receive the same prompt, model configuration, decoding settings and budget, with one attempt each. Record the exact source revision, skill digest, provider/model version, response bytes and provenance in a new input before scoring. This repository does not include a live model-run transport or an independently reviewed answer for these held-out cases. All twelve attempts are explicitly unavailable and all six expected answers are `expected-unreviewed`; the included run measures harness coverage, **not** method accuracy.

The runner accepts recorded responses only when they have action ID, mechanism and ordered schedule. It compares exact strings and ordered schedules, and counts finding false alarms and misses on reviewed cases. A supplied review claim and artifact digest are input provenance, not cryptographic proof that the reviewer was independent; the caller must verify the review artifact outside this runner. In particular, the existing incident fixtures in T03b, T04 and T05 are also `expected-unreviewed` and are not included in any accuracy denominator. Exact-string scoring is a narrow measure and may reject a semantically equivalent answer. Report the raw responses and any semantic adjudication separately; never edit the expected answers to improve a score.

An External bot or External bot workflow can run the command as a closed-input local step, save stdout in its own append-only evidence store, and branch on an input error without stopping unrelated delivery. The scoring result grants no authority to merge or publish. Six synthetic cases cannot estimate real-world error rates, and a zero scored denominator provides no comparison between arms.
